chunks: Ahmad ibn Mihrān narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl, who said:

Al-Makhzūmī narrated to me—and his mother was from the descendants of Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib (عليه السلام). He said: Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā (عليه السلام) sent for us, so he gathered us and then said to us, “Do you know why I invited you?” We said, “No.”

So he said: “Bear witness that this son of mine is my waṣī, the one who will undertake my affair, and my khalīfah after me. Whoever has a debt owed by me, let him take it from this son of mine. Whoever has been promised something by me, let him have it fulfilled through him. And whoever has no alternative but to meet me, then let him not meet me except with his letter.”

key_terms.الْقَيِّمُ بِأَمْرِي: the one who will manage and uphold my affairs
key_terms.بِكِتَابِهِ: with his written authorization or letter
key_terms.دَيْنٌ: a debt owed and to be repaid
key_terms.عِدَةٌ: a promise or commitment due for fulfillment

ai.seo_question: How did Imām Mūsā al-Kāẓim (عليه السلام) designate Imām al-Riḍā (عليه السلام) as his successor?
ai.summary: This hadith records Imām Mūsā al-Kāẓim (عليه السلام) publicly identifying his son as his waṣī, the one responsible for his affairs, and his khalīfah after him. It also shows the transfer of practical and financial responsibilities to him, indicating recognized religious authority and succession.
